topic: The Great Depression and New Deal

question.leadin: One theory suggests that this woman and Fred Noonan died in the Mariana Islands while in Japanese custody.
question.text: Name this female aviator who left New Guinea aboard her plane, the Electra, but never arrived at Howland Island, which has spawned many theories about her disappearance.
question.clue: One theory surrounding the whereabouts of this person and their companion, Fred Noonan, was that they were executed by Japanese soldiers on Saipan.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about famous campaign slogans.
swap.text: This man used the slogan "a chicken in every pot, a car in every garage," which Democrats mocked him for in the 1932 election after his poor handling of the Great Depression.
swap.clue: He established the Reconstruction Finance Corporation while in office, and one of his opponents declared "there is nothing in but jelly" in response to his order for Douglas MacArthur to break up the Bonus Army.

question.leadin: Give the following about attempts to ease the Great Depression.
question.text: This 1933 law, named for two Democratic senators, created the FDIC. It also notably forbade commercial banks from many investment activities, a measure repealed in 1999.
question.answerHtml: Glass-Steagall Act (prompt on "Banking Act of 1933;” accept logical equivalents for Act, including Bill and Law)
question.clue: A reenactment of this legislation was the subject of the Volcker Plan.

swap.text: This U.S. First Lady resigned from the D.A.R. in 1939 in protest of the group's racist decision to preventMarian Anderson from performing at its concert hall in Washington, D.C.
swap.clue: During her time as First Lady, she wrote a newspaper column called "My Day," and was asked to serve as a delegate to the UN General Assembly in 1946 by President Truman.

question.text: During this 1929 event carried out on Capone's orders, perpetrated with Thompson submachine guns, several men disguised themselves as police officers and shot 7 of Bugs Moran's associates.
question.clue: The victims of this event had been tricked into believing that they were waiting for a delivery of stolen whiskey.

swap.text: This New Deal agency provided unemployed men with jobs relating to natural resources, such as planting trees and improving irrigation.
swap.clue: Employees of this organization were organized into camps and often lived in tents.

question.leadin: Answer the following questions about Francis Townsend.
question.text: Later on, Townsend created the Union Party along with Gerald L. K. Smith and this Detroit-based Catholic priest. This priest used his radio program and newspaper, Social Justice, to spread his antisemitic views.
question.clue: This man established the National Shrine of the Little Flower Basilica in Royal Oak, Michigan.

swap.text: Al Capone is widely believed to be the one behind this 1929 killing of seven members of the rival gang North Side Irish.

question.leadin: Identify the following about some so-called "armies" from American history.
question.text: In 1932, these thousands of World War I veterans, led by Walter Waters, descended on Washington to demand payment for their wartime service.
question.clue: It protested a bill that was proposed by Wright Patman by embarking on a "death march" to Capitol Hill.

swap.leadin: Answer these questions concerning the medallion that is awarded to inductees to the National Inventors Hall of Fame.
swap.text: The reverse side of the medallion sites this section of Article I of the Constitution, establishing the American patent system.

question.text: The one and only North Dakotan ever to run for President, this candidate of Father Coughlin's Union Party polled 900,000 votes in the 1936 election after being drafted as a last-minute replacement for the assassinated Huey Long.
question.clue: After Long died, the Union Party ran this North Dakotan for President in 1936. He sponsored a mortgage refinancing act for farmers along with Lynn Frazier.

swap.leadin: This politician campaigned for governor with the slogan "Every man a king, but no one wears a crown."
swap.text: Name this Louisiana politician, nicknamed "The Kingfish," who proposed the "Share Our Wealth" program as a senator. This politician was assassinated by Carl Weiss just prior to a likely run in the 1936 presidential election.
swap.clue: This politician imagined winning the presidency in his book My First Days in the White House.

question.text: This politician called Standard Oil "foreign murderers" for their perceived role in the Gran Chaco War. Conflict over oil taxes led a "Square Deal Association" opposing this politician to seize a Baton Rouge courthouse.
question.answerHtml: Huey Long [or Huey Pierce Long, Jr.; accept the Kingfish]
question.clue: He joined the Senate in 1932 in name only, not traveling to Washington for years.

swap.leadin: A group of this many Black students in Rock Hill, South Carolina, pioneered the "Jail, No Bail" strategy after being arrested at a sit-in.
swap.text: What number also appears in the most common name of a 1972 anti-discrimination provision in education authored primarily by Patsy Mink?
swap.answerHtml: nine [accept Title IX; accept Friendship Nine or Rock Hill Nine]
swap.clue: Countee Cullen wrote about a group of this many people that ends "Surely, I said, / Now will the poets sing. / But they have raised no cry. / I wonder why."

question.leadin: Answer these questions about the New Deal FTPE.
question.text: General Hugh Johnson was made the director of this agency, which was created by an act that set up a group of fair competition codes for industry.
question.clue: The business community soured on the 1933 law creating this agency, which was directed by Hugh Samuel Johnson and symbolized with a blue eagle. The "sick chicken" case, Schechter v. US, eliminated it.

swap.text: This man, FDR's Interior secretary for his entire presidency, was the director of the Public Works Administration. This man often bickered with Harry Hopkins, director of the Works Progress Administration.
swap.clue: One person with this last name chaired Bill Clinton's 1992 presidential campaign and was nicknamed the "Garbage Man" by (+) Michael Lewis in an unflattering 1997 profile.

question.leadin: During a vote on Charles Warren's nomination for attorney general, this man made a mad dash across Washington in a taxi cab to break the tie, becoming the subject of a parody of "Paul Revere's Ride."
question.text: Name this vice president, the devisor of a namesake plan following WWI, whose scathing inaugural speech against the rules of the Senate was one of the many reasons that his superior, Calvin Coolidge, hated him.
question.clue: This U.S. Vice President who was succeeded in that position in 1929 by Charles Curtis.

swap.leadin: John Hart Ely's Democracy and Distrust builds on Justice Harlan Stone's opinion in this case by arguing that the Warren Court's activism was not values-based but process-based.
swap.text: Name this Supreme Court case, whose Footnote Four introduced the basis for strict scrutiny by proposing a "narrower scope for operation of the presumption of constitutionality."
swap.clue: This 1938 Supreme Court case, which is more famous for its "footnote four."

question.leadin: Tom McCoy was a principal actor in this event, which in the span of a single day used the favorable results of a recount to reorganize the entire government of Rhode Island.
question.text: Identify this pivotal event of Rhode Island history which took place on January 1, 1935, and in which a possible case of voter fraud allowed Democrats to assume complete control of state politics.

swap.text: This man was the first director of the NRA and Time's Man of the Year in 1933. He called for a "blanket code" including a minimum wage, maximum workweek, and abolition of child labor, but was fired in 1934 after handing out leaflets praising Mussolini's "Corporate State."
